requirement_summary: Beacon Protection Enabled is described as one setting for all affiliated APs of an AP MLD (no 'shall').

requirement_summary: Affiliated APs of an AP MLD advertise the same RSNE/RSNXE except the AKM list and MFPR, and share at least one AKM.
notes: SEC.MLD_COMMON_SUITES checks the RSNE half, SEC.MLD_SAME_RSNXE the RSNXE half (#95). Read strictly: once one link includes an RSNXE, every link advertises the same one. Run 1794875139 (runs/experiments/, a labeled negative experiment) shows hostapd advertising RSNXE 0x20 on a [SAE-EXT-KEY, OWE] link and none on an [OWE] link.

requirement_summary: For MLO the client sends one RSNE whose AKM, pairwise and group cipher are common to all affiliated APs; a client with no overlap declines.
The AP MLD compares MFPC/MFPR per requested link to decide which links it accepts.
notes: P0 has one PMF setting for the whole AP MLD, so per-link MFPC/MFPR differences can't be expressed. Strength not recorded in the research; check the PDF if this becomes a rule.

requirement_summary: RSNA rekeying for MLO: the AP MLD manages the PTKSA, each affiliated AP its own group keys; a new PTKSA should be set up before the old one expires.
notes: Only a 'should' (recommendation), which the strength vocabulary has no value for: no requirement a candidate can break. Recorded as the caveat on the rekey interval dimensions (runs/smoke/README.md). Was OUT_OF_SCOPE until NO_RULE existed (#75). Checked by Michelle, in the PDF, 2026-11-24 (#109): the amendment to 802.11-2024 §12.6.19 has no 'shall'. It adds that a non-AP MLD may reassociate with the same AP MLD and/or set up a new RSNA when a PTKSA is deleted (a permission), that the AP MLD's Authenticator manages packet number assignment for the PTKSA and each affiliated AP's for its link's group keys, with group key updates per link through a group key handshake between the MLDs, and extends the 'should' on a new PTKSA to MLDs.

requirement_summary: ML security: one PTKSA across the setup links, and a GTKSA/IGTKSA/BIGTKSA per link; different links use different group keys.

The single PTKSA is why a PTK rekey after link_remove still concerns the remaining link (contrast C1). Per-link group keys would be a behavior check, not modeled. requirement_summary: At the removal TBTT a non-AP MLD considers the removed AP's link nonexistent and deletes what it kept for it; a non-AP MLD with two setup links keeps the other one (NOTE 7).
notes: A requirement on the client's behavior, not on a candidate. After link_remove the client keeps link 0 and the one PTKSA (§35.3.5.2), and an Authenticator may rekey the PTK (802.11-2024 §12.6.19), so nothing read makes a 5 s PTK rekey with link_remove illegal: both sides of contrast C1 stay legal. The runs show the client's EAPOL-Key replies not reaching hostapd after LINK_REMOVE; where they're lost isn't in the logs, and no claim is made. Read by Claude in the PDF text, 2026-11-17 (#75); not yet checked by a person.
